title: Struggling for fifteen years and the failed move to California
summary: After Condon's he finds the music sliding, struggles, and moves to the West Coast, where cafe owners pay only union scale.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: We're now talking about the period of after about 15 years --

About a 15 year period of real tough going. I mean struggling, not just--- you sort of had to struggle to make it and I know I wasn't alone, because all those guys from that period were struggling with me. And,they were hit and miss propositions and I thought - at one point - that I would be very smart maybe

to move to the West Coast and, of course, that was the worst thing I could have done; that's the one place I had a good offer to go out there and after I got there, it didn't last very long and, uh, first of all, they didn't want to pay any money and, uh, of course, I could understand why all those cafe owners out there -- you see, when the days when the jazz guys were working in the studios and in the theaters, you know, and the sound studios making movies; they were making good money doing that but when they liked to play jazz, they would book themselves in some of these clubs and work cheap. And, those guys out there got the idea that everybody worked cheap and it's a very sad scene because they couldn't care whether you were a double Louie Armstrong; they pay the union scale and that's what you're going to get and the union scale, as you know, is not livable -- you cannot make it on the union scale unless you have a lot of extra work on the side and all that kind of stuff.
